newsitem.title: INDIA: India's biggest bank H1 96/97 net seen up sharply.
newsitem.headline: India's biggest bank H1 96/97 net seen up sharply.

text.p: Profits of India's biggest bank, State Bank of India (SBI) is seen rising sharply in first half of 1996/97 (April-March), a Reuters poll of major brokerages showed on Tuesday.

The state-owned bank, whose net profit is projected to leap by 178 percent in the six-month period, is expected be the most outstanding performer among the 30 firms making up the Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) benchmark index, the poll found.
The Reuters poll of 14 securities firms forecast that the 30 index companies would record an average growth of 20.64 percent in net profit and 16.48 percent in sales.
SBI, which controls over 20 percent market share of total banking deposits and advances -- will see its incomes rise by a projected 22.5 percent, analysts said.

They said SBI's net profit would improve despite a fall in its advances, its main source of income. Bank advances fell by around 22 billion rupees ($616 million) in the first four months of 1996/97 due to poor credit demand from industry, they said.
Reduced provision for depreciation in the market value of securities would be the major factor in boosting SBI's bottomline, analysts said.

"SBI had to provide more than eight billion rupees towards depreciation on the market value of its investments in government securities in the first half of 1995/96," said Prasanna Someshwar, banking analyst at W.I. Carr.
"Besides, another two billion rupees had to be provided last year towards wage arrears to its employees, consequent upon a wage revision."
The absence of these two provisions alone would be enough to boost SBI's profit this year, he said.
Analysts also said SBI was better equipped to withstand any pressure on its spreads.
"The share of fee-based income in its total income has been rising," said Dick Mody, banking analyst at ICICI Securities and Finance Company. "This will protect it if spreads are squeezed."
Other strengths of the bank include a country-wide network of more than 8,000 branches which enable it to tap deposits from sources inaccesible to other banks, analysts said.

The bank is also in the process of raising $400 million through an issue of global depositary receipts (GDRs). The first roadshow for the issue was held on September 21. This would provide additional cheap funds to the bank, analysts said.
